video_title: Nvidia, We Need to Talk | Protect the Pile Episode 32
gist: Hedgeye Asset Management's panel argues a strengthening dollar and slowing global liquidity (below nominal GDP) are driving a Quad 4-like volatility regime; the real Nvidia story is chip diversion to China via shell companies, with guidance, leadership and a 2027 hyperscaler capex peak as risks around its earnings and the Anthropic IPO. They favor low-revenue-volatility subscription businesses (MSCI, Nasdaq, Moody's, S&P Global) and housing over pricey 'safety' like Walmart.

themes.theme: Dollar/rates squeeze and fading global liquidity

insights.claim: As of Nov 13, the S&P 500 was around 7,520, about 3.6-3.7% off its all-time high, while the 10-year Treasury yield had rebounded to ~5.13% after hitting a multi-decade high of 5.30% weeks earlier, unwinding a brief 'rates coming down' narrative that had lifted housing.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Housing/rate-sensitive rallies built on falling-yield narratives are fragile while the 10-year sits above 5%.

insights.claim: The US dollar rallied roughly 2-3% in a very short period, and the panel views dollar strength as a direct drag on global dollar liquidity at a time when most major central banks, including the Fed, are effectively tightening.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: A strengthening dollar tightens global liquidity; expect weakness in credit, vol spikes and pressure on anything fragile.
insights.quote: the dollar strengthening doesn't help

insights.claim: RPK's global liquidity measure grew at a mid-teens year-over-year rate earlier in the year but has slowed to sub-8% y/y, and the more important 1/3/6-month annualized rates have slowed dramatically and are now well below nominal GDP.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Liquidity growth below nominal GDP implies assets must be liquidated to fund the economy; watch short-window annualized liquidity, not lagging y/y.
insights.quote: what matters more is that sort of one month, three month, six month annualize, like what's happening at the margin

insights.claim: When liquidity growth runs below nominal GDP, either assets get sold to fund activity, GDP contracts, or money supply must increase; RPK argues liquidity must turn up to change the market story.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Treat a re-acceleration in liquidity (or central bank easing) as the key regime-change signal before getting aggressive.

insights.claim: The dollar and rates moves were one-directional for five to six sessions in a row, which is rare for markets of that size and likely to create ripple effects and forced shakeouts.
insights.speaker: panelist
insights.so_what: Persistent one-way moves in deep macro markets often precede deleveraging elsewhere.

insights.claim: A panelist found it alarming that Treasury Secretary Bessent went on TV touting how well the last four Treasury auctions went, reading it as a sign of official nervousness about funding demand.
insights.speaker: panelist
insights.so_what: Official reassurance on auction demand can be a tell of funding stress; watch auction tails and term premium.
insights.quote: If you're just even saying that out loud, I'm nervous.

insights.claim: Higher long rates and wider credit spreads raise the financing cost of the AI capex buildout, which could produce a second-derivative slowdown in the rate of AI spending next year.
insights.speaker: panelist
insights.so_what: Watch credit spreads and duration as leading indicators of AI capex growth deceleration.

insights.claim: The 2018 analog: US equities held up against slowing dollar liquidity while EM was already crushed, then US markets broke late in the year until Powell's 180-degree pivot right before Christmas improved liquidity at the margin and the market bottomed.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: A Fed pivot may be the catalyst needed to end the current drawdown; until then, slowing liquidity favors defense.
insights.quote: Powell did a total 180 um right before Christmas and like and suddenly the market bottomed

themes.theme: Volatility regime, positioning and pod-driven factor sloshing

insights.claim: Tech has seen repeated Friday selling days that look like forced liquidations from funds, and Tier 1 data reportedly shows dealer gamma is negative, amplifying moves in both directions.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Negative gamma means larger intraday swings; size positions for higher realized vol.
insights.quote: isn't the tier one data showing gammers negative?

insights.claim: Prime broker data (e.g., Goldman) shows positioning being wiped clean, and Sam thinks many funds have written off this year and will reposition for next year starting in the second half of November, which ironically could set up an upside surprise.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Clean positioning plus year-end apathy can fuel a surprise rally; watch late-November repositioning.

insights.claim: Sam worries that the Washington administration is consumed by corruption, finger-pointing and pardon fights, so the usual government/Fed 'bumpers' that dampen market volatility are absent.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Don't count on a policy put in the near term; volatility may persist without official guidance.
insights.quote: this clown show in DC they are so wrapped up in a hornet's nest of corruption fingerpointing

insights.claim: Insurance stocks outperforming is likely less about fundamentals (P&C pricing a bit better) and more 'lily pad jumping' by financials pod managers who must stay long something within their sector while avoiding banks (credit spreads widening) and brokers (tough IPO comps).
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Outperformance driven by pod constraints can reverse fast when flows shift; don't mistake it for a fundamental story.
insights.quote: what I really think it is is just a lily pad jumping

insights.claim: Apple's outperformance within tech is largely a pairs-trade artifact: managers shorting AI-exposed tech need to be long something in tech, and Apple is the natural offset, similar to the old long Exxon/short E&Ps energy pod trade.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Apple's relative strength is flow-driven and could unwind when the AI short trade reverses.

insights.claim: With tech roughly 40% of the S&P 500, buying the equal-weight index (RSP) is effectively selling tech to buy the field, so equal-weight versus cap-weight performance is a market-level version of the same factor rotation.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Track RSP vs SPX as a gauge of whether re-entering capital avoids tech.

insights.claim: If the Anthropic IPO clears, returning cash may go into non-tech parts of the market rather than tech, favoring the equal-weighted/broader market over mega-cap tech.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Positioning for broadening (equal weight) may beat chasing tech after the IPO.

insights.claim: Sam floats that the Anthropic IPO actually raising money and becoming public next week could be one of the few catalysts to calm the volatility regime, regardless of first-day trading.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: A successful raise could ease AI funding fears; watch pricing Wednesday night.

insights.claim: RPK leans toward the Anthropic IPO being a sell-the-news event given the slowing liquidity backdrop, arguing it won't fix problems like CoreWeave or high-yield spreads.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Be wary of a one-day relief rally around the IPO; underlying credit stress in AI infra persists.
insights.quote: that didn't fix core weave, you know, high yield um spreads

insights.claim: Private AI funding has been walking down: Anthropic's valuation was marked down, and OpenAI was supposed to raise $30 billion, cut it to $20 billion, and finally closed on $15 billion.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Shrinking private AI rounds signal capital scarcity for AI; read-through to AI infrastructure spend.
insights.quote: OpenAI was supposed to raise 30 billion. It went to 20 billion. They finally closed on 15.

insights.claim: RPK says the Anthropic IPO feels like a hype job: repeated Bloomberg headlines of 'six times oversubscribed' are meaningless because investors routinely inflate orders, even broken deals claim oversubscription, ~20 banks are on the deal, and Fidelity is relaxing IPO restrictions to push it to retail.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Broad retail distribution and headline-oversubscription marketing are classic late-cycle IPO tells; be skeptical of aftermarket demand.
insights.quote: We are moving this in front of anyone with two coins to rub together is being shot this deal.

themes.theme: Nvidia China-diversion scandal and leadership change

insights.claim: RPK argues the real Nvidia story is not the salacious personal angles but that chips were sold through shell companies to banned Chinese buyers, and he expects multiple more shell companies to surface.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Regulatory/legal liability and a potential revenue reset are the key risks, not the headline drama.
insights.quote: They were selling stuff through shell companies to the Chinese

insights.claim: Nvidia was posting $70-80 billion per quarter in international sales while China kept pace in AI, implying a far larger share of that revenue ended up in China than reported.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: International revenue is at risk if diversion channels are closed; scrutinize regional mix.
insights.quote: they've been putting up 70 to 80 billion per quarter in international sales

insights.claim: Nvidia's incremental gross margins at one point ran around 99%, which RPK suggests may partly reflect buyers willing to pay any price because they could flip chips at a profit to restricted end-users.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Pricing power may be partly a gray-market artifact; margin normalization risk if that demand disappears.
insights.quote: the incrementals on like gross margin at one point were running like 99%

insights.claim: RPK says he questioned years ago how China could compete in AI if everyone needs Nvidia chips while China supposedly lacked them, calling those mutually exclusive claims, and cites DeepSeek's origin at a Chinese hedge fund with questions about its GPU access.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: The China AI competitiveness puzzle now has an answer that implicates Nvidia's sales channels.

insights.claim: Sam notes it is not yet clear whether chips reached China itself or were funneled via Singapore/Malaysia shell companies into Southeast Asian data centers and neoclouds owned (sometimes invisibly) by Chinese hyperscalers; since training can occur anywhere, location matters less than access.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Expect scrutiny of Southeast Asian data-center demand, a key driver of Nvidia's non-US sales.

insights.claim: The investigation will likely hinge on who approved shipments: if Jensen shipped without Commerce approval it is very bad for Nvidia; if Commerce approved, it is very bad for Lutnick.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Liability allocation between Nvidia and Commerce determines the size of legal/financial blowback.
insights.quote: Did did Jensen send stuff without commerce approval which would be really bad or did they did did they get approval uh from the commerce department which for Lutnik is really [laughter] bad.

insights.claim: RPK links the scandal to a crypto venture (recalled only as 'world financial something') that received a reported ~$500 million from the UAE while lobbying occurred to let the UAE import Nvidia chips, predicting a 'Panama Papers moment' revealing many shell companies.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Political-entanglement risk could widen the probe and hit Gulf AI chip deals.
insights.quote: it's like a Panama papers moment

insights.claim: Sam compares Nvidia without Jensen to Apple pre/post Jobs: roadmaps are baked for ~two years, but Jensen's personality likely swayed supply-chain deals others couldn't.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Near-term execution may hold, but long-run deal-making and roadmap ambition are at risk.

insights.claim: If regulators now scrutinize where Nvidia's chips actually land, the valuation equation becomes a 'whole different conversation'.
insights.speaker: John McNamera
insights.so_what: End-use verification could permanently lower addressable demand and the multiple.

themes.theme: Nvidia earnings setup and the 2027 capex peak

insights.claim: Nvidia reports Tuesday night, the day before Anthropic is expected to price Wednesday night; the panel expects business-as-usual guidance because books closed before the scandal broke and a cut ahead of the IPO would be a disaster.
insights.speaker: panel
insights.so_what: Event sequencing: Nvidia print is the first test; a surprise cut would derail the IPO.

insights.claim: RPK believes Nvidia is at significant risk of cutting revenue guidance on international sales weakness this quarter or next, though Sam would be surprised if it happens this quarter.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Position for a later-quarter guide-down on international sales rather than an immediate one.
insights.quote: I do think we're at significant risk of them cutting revenue guidance on international sales weakness at some point

insights.claim: Even without the scandal, Sam sees calendar 2028 as potentially Nvidia's first year of top-line rate-of-change decline (visible to the market in 2027) because hyperscaler capex likely peaks on an absolute basis in 2027 and its growth slows sharply in 2028.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Nvidia is a cyclical; the market should start discounting the 2027 capex peak well before it arrives.
insights.quote: 2028 calendar 2028 for this company is potentially kind of the first year of that rate of change decline in top line

insights.claim: A permanent successor CEO (Colette or whoever follows) is expected to 'clear the decks' and must re-diligence all sales arrangements and financing deals, putting Nvidia's handshake backstops and promises to customers in question.
insights.speaker: panel
insights.so_what: Kitchen-sink risk and potential unwinding of vendor-financing/backstop commitments across the AI ecosystem.
insights.quote: you got to you're walking into this thing, you're gonna be like, I need to see the terms on everything on every one of the deals we struck

insights.claim: Sam expects Nvidia to punt questions on Asia revenue share and to keep its line, previously stated by CFO Colette Kress (transcribed 'Colette Crest'), that everything sold in Asia was approved by the US government.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Lack of disclosure on Asia mix will keep the overhang alive after the print.

themes.theme: Positioning for Quad 4: low-volatility revenue and housing

insights.claim: Hedgeye research expects several back-to-back quarters of Quad 4 (decelerating growth and inflation) into early next year, and tightening liquidity already has the market acting Quad 4-like even though the current quad is closer to Quad 2.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Tilt toward Quad 4 playbook: defensives, falling-rate beneficiaries, away from cyclicals and high beta.

insights.claim: Buying 'safety' like Walmart at 43x earnings only works if money stays in the casino; in Quad 4 valuation matters, and low beta can hide risk, as when SaaS stocks with ~0.7 betas in 2021 still fell ~65% the next year.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Expensive low-beta defensives are not real protection; screen on valuation too.
insights.quote: Walmart at 43 times earnings

insights.claim: Sam's protection framework: seek businesses with low revenue volatility and high-90% subscription renewal rates, beyond obvious staples and healthcare; software used to qualify but now faces AI disruption.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Information/business-services subscription models offer defensiveness without sector-label crowding.

insights.claim: Specific low-volatility subscription names cited: MSCI (index data and analytics), Nasdaq (data services plus volume-driven trading), and Moody's (MCO) and S&P Global (SPGI), which pair cyclical ratings with steady index/data businesses; Josh Steiner has MCO and SPGI as bullish recommendations, and payment companies were also flagged.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Candidates for Quad 4 defense: steady 6-9% growers whose revenue revisions should hold up.
insights.quote: nobody's going to pull the plug on their subscriptions

insights.claim: Housing and housing-related stocks are the inverse-cyclical opportunity: cheap and out of favor for years, with potentially substantial positive revision changes if rates fall meaningfully.
insights.speaker: Sam Ramen
insights.so_what: Housing offers cheap upside convexity to a real rate decline, complementing pricey stable names.

insights.claim: RPK's screen: low volatility of revenue and EBIT over time, average-to-below-average valuation, and dividend payers; low-vol/high-dividend is already working, though rising yields pressure the dividend leg until Quad 4 delivers both slowing revenue and falling rates.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Low-vol dividend strategies should work best once yields roll over in Quad 4.

insights.claim: RPK stresses the market sits at an all-time-high market cap to GDP and a CAPE ratio at prior bubble levels; not a timing tool, but it shifts the goal toward competitive returns when upside plays fail.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Prioritize downside-resilient returns over upside chasing at bubble-level valuations.

insights.claim: On oil, Brent and WTI are hovering at trade/trend levels with renewed Strait of Hormuz tensions; RPK still favors a straddle view that oil ends a lot higher or a lot lower but not at current levels.
insights.speaker: Patrick Hen (RPK)
insights.so_what: Long-volatility (straddle) exposure in crude fits a binary geopolitical setup.
insights.quote: It's either going to be a lot higher or a lot lower, but it probably isn't here.
